newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyushu Electric scraps Kushima nuclear plant plant.
newsitem.headline: Kyushu Electric scraps Kushima nuclear plant plant.

text.p: Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc said on Tuesday it has abandoned a plan to build a nuclear power plant in the southern Japanese city of Kushima due to local opposition.

The electric utility started preliminary studies on constructing a plant in Kushima in 1994 after an invitation from the municipal assembly. It suspended the research in 1995 after a majority in the assembly turned against the plan, a Kyushu Electric spokesman said.
Media reports said Kyushu Electric decided to scrap the plan to build the plant because it expected a majority would vote against it in a referendum planned for the summer.
Kushima mayor Shigeru Yamashita was elected for a third term last year on a pledge to hold the referendum.
A city official said it would be held as scheduled, despite the scrapping of the plan to build the plant.
Last year, the town of Maki in northern Japan carried out a similar referendum on Tohoku Electric Power Co Inc's plan to build a nuclear power plant, and returned a majority "no" vote.

Though the result of the referendum was not legally binding, Maki mayor Takaaki Sasaguchi decided not to sell town land to the power firm after the vote, effectively halting Tohoku Electric's quarter-century-old plan to build a nuclear power plant in the town.
